cells.tense: You are standing on ground you chose and holding it, with the pen in your hand right now
cells.act: mark the good thing together, out loud
cells.ask: When something you've been holding ground for actually lands, say so out loud to whoever's nearby — just the fact of it, not the long defense behind it.
cells.core:
You can hold a direction in the half-lit part of things. Not blindly — there's pressure, there's resistance, and you keep going anyway. You've gathered what was scattered into one clear line. The path ahead is still only lit a step at a time, and you don't need more than that. With the pen in your hand, you're still writing.

The useful thing here isn't to stop holding. It's to look at who's on this stretch with you and say what's good, out loud, while it's happening. Not after. Not in a recap. The weight you're carrying gets lighter when it's shared mid-step, and the people with you can feel where the ground actually is. Say it now, while it's live, and the momentum goes further than defending it alone would.
cells.sheetLine: You can hold a direction in the half-lit part without forcing the whole road.
cells.verb: Gathering what was scattered and holding one chosen direction against pressure, on a road you can't see past the next step
cells.place: A stretch of half-lit path where the way forward only shows itself one step at a time

cells.tense: You are bracing for the next stretch before the ground under you has shown its shape
cells.act: let the mind rest instead of working the problem
cells.ask: For an hour, don't solve the stretch you can't see yet. Not a break from work — set it aside and let your mind have nothing to fix.
cells.core:
The strain in you is running past the road. You're gathering for a defense that hasn't arrived, bracing against resistance nobody's actually put on you yet. Every half-lit stretch gets solved in advance, and the solving is heavier than the walking would be. Somewhere in there the sheer work of holding has crowded out the direction it was meant to serve.

What's thin isn't the effort. It's the quiet that lets you feel which way you're actually pointed. Let it be unsolved for a while. Don't redraw your plan. Sit with the ambiguity you've been trying to outrun, and let your mind calibrate to something other than the next threat. The choice you make once you're rested will come from you, not from the bracing. That's what holding ground is for — to keep you pointed, not to keep you clenched.
cells.sheetLine: You're solving a stretch you haven't reached yet. Stop for an hour.
cells.verb: Gathering what was scattered and holding one chosen direction against pressure, on a road you can't see past the next step
cells.place: A stretch of half-lit path where the way forward only shows itself one step at a time

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door you already walked through, holding a direction that has moved on without you
cells.act: keep what the change produced from drifting
cells.ask: Find one thing the ending left you — a new rhythm, a cleared space, something that took — and do a small thing that holds it where it is.
cells.core:
Something worth protecting already came through, and the effort to keep it stopped before the thing did. You're standing at a door that's behind you. The half-lit path keeps asking for the next step, and nothing in you is laying it — not because you can't, but because the last stretch used everything and you're still there. The strength hasn't gone. It's just aimed at ground you've already covered.

What the ending produced is still lying around, unkept. Find one piece you can see — a new rhythm, a cleared space, something that took — and do a small thing today that holds it where it is. Not a big move. Not a new direction. Just the quiet work of keeping what already changed from drifting back. Something real to hold is what the stalled part of you needs, so the next step has ground under it again.
cells.sheetLine: The ending already gave you something. One small act keeps it.
cells.verb: Gathering what was scattered and holding one chosen direction against pressure, on a road you can't see past the next step
cells.place: A stretch of half-lit path where the way forward only shows itself one step at a time

cells.tense: The ground you stand on was shaped by your own effort, and you describe it as land you happened upon
cells.act: build the first new thing from what the clearing showed
cells.ask: Make one new thing with your hands — nothing depends on it, nobody's asking for it — because starting is what you do.
cells.core:
The direction you're holding was authored by you. You gathered what was scattered and pointed it where it points. From inside the pressure, it reads as the situation you're in, not the work you did. The half-lit path looks like land you found. It isn't. It's what you made.

Before you were holding ground for something, you started things because starting is what you do. That earlier act — taking a direction with no guarantee and walking it — is still you. Begin something small this week. Nothing rides on it, no one needs it, and the road under your feet will show the old footprints. It reads differently once you remember the building.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim in my draft is that the person is actively reading the room or timing celebrations — the record only says Resolve is holding ground on ambiguous terrain, and I let that imply social vigilance. A reader could reasonably say the strain is private and internal, not about other people at all; nothing in the draw requires the pressure to be social. The ask survives either way because 'let the mind rest instead of working the problem' is useful whether the overwork is about others' reactions or about a decision with no map. The sentence that serves me more than them is the one that makes the whole thing sound like a social performance problem — it flatters my reading and pins a motive on them, so I cut it.
